summary:
SELENE NAVIGATOR – Making Lunar Mission Planning More Accessible
SELENE NAVIGATOR is an interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to help young engineers, students, and small teams explore and understand the challenges of planning missions to the Moon.
Using publicly available NASA and international space-agency datasets, the platform brings key mission-planning considerations into one workspace. Users can explore the entire Moon in 3D, investigate potential landing sites, examine terrain and sunlight conditions, understand communication visibility, compare locations, and experiment with mission timelines and rover routes.
Lunar exploration involves complex decisions that require both scientific understanding and engineering considerations. SELENE NAVIGATOR aims to make these concepts easier to explore by providing an accessible starting point for developing early mission ideas.
It also encourages teams to connect different mission requirements, evaluate trade-offs, and understand how individual decisions can influence an overall mission plan.
Rather than replacing professional mission-planning systems, it encourages users to learn, experiment, evaluate possibilities, and think through the challenges of operating on the lunar surface.
Our vision is to make lunar mission planning more approachable and give the next generation of space explorers the opportunity to think and plan like engineers.
details: SeleneNavigator is an interactive web suite built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that uses a 3D lunar globe, 2D descent simulator, and multi-criteria scoring to evaluate Artemis candidate landing zones at the lunar south pole. It streamlines mission planning by combining real-time solar and Earth communication tracking, dynamic priority sliders, and instant JSON, CSV, or PDF data exports into a single browser-based tool. By pinpointing sunlit crater ridges right next to water-ice-rich permanently shadowed regions, the project aims to accelerate sustainable lunar exploration and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) while making real planetary science accessible to everyone. Built and hosted on GitHub Pages using standard web technologies, the platform integrates live NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris geometry alongside multi-mission datasets from NASA LRO, ISRO’s Chandrayaan-3, JAXA’s Kaguya, and KASA’s ShadowCam. Its creative edge comes from gamifying raw elevation rasters into a hands-on 2D landing simulator, matching lunar zones to real terrestrial analog testbeds across six space agencies, and packaging complex telemetry into a judge-ready guided walkthrough. Throughout development, our team carefully weighed solar illumination duty cycles, Direct-to-Earth radio visibility, terrain slope and boulder hazards, and cryogenic water-ice stability—while transparently accounting for scientific caveats like crater-wall shadowing and subsurface drilling needs.
